meta_description: HireSignal interviews every applicant with an adaptive AI interview and sends your team a scored report with the evidence behind it. Part of Kuma Group.
how_title: A CV tells you what they wrote. The interview tells you what they *know*.
how_lede: This happens with every applicant, the same way, at any hour. Nobody on your team has to be on the call.
how_s1_p: One link per role, or one per person. They start when it suits them.
how_s2_p: An interview in {languages} that asks again when an answer is thin.
how_s3_p: Contradictions, rehearsed answers, tricks in the CV. Flagged with their own words.
how_s4_p: In your inbox when they finish. Eight dimensions, each backed by what they said.
how_s5_p: Ranked by role, requirements checked. The decision stays with you.
how_note: An example for an administrative role. Names are invented. It works the same way for yours.
m_mail_body: Hi Maria, thanks for applying. Your interview takes about 15 minutes. Start whenever you are ready.
m_q1: You managed calendars for three directors. What happened the last time two of them wanted the same slot?
m_a1: I moved the internal meeting, kept the one with the client, and told both assistants before lunch.
m_q2: How did the director whose meeting moved take it?
m_sig1_q: Said she booked all the travel, later said an agency handled it.
m_sig2_q: Moved supply orders to twice a month and saved about $400 a month.
m_sig3: Script risk low. French assessed: advanced.
m_sig4: CV alert: text written for the AI, not for you
change_r1_a: The ones someone has time to call
change_r2_a: Office hours, when calendars line up
change_r2_b: Any hour, in the applicant's own time zone
change_r3_a: Shifts with the interviewer and the day
change_r3_b: The same rubric for every applicant
change_r4_a: Judged by ear, if someone on the team speaks it
change_r4_b: Assessed in the interview, with a level in the report
change_r5_a: Caught if the interviewer happens to notice
change_r5_b: Contradictions, rehearsed answers and CV tricks, each with the quote
change_r6_b: A report, the evidence behind it and the full transcript
sample_lede: This is what lands in your inbox. The applicant is fictional, played by a second AI. The interview and the report are real HireSignal output, unedited.
sample_c1_p: Advance, worth a review, or weak fit. Hard requirements are checked apart from the score.
sample_c2_p: Every score comes with the reasoning and the applicant's own words.
sample_c3_p: When two answers can't both be true, you see both quotes.
sample_c4_p: If a CV hides instructions for the AI, the report tells you and quotes them.
sample_c5_p: The full transcript is attached, so you can check anything yourself.

cfg_meta_title: Try HireSignal: set up your interview
cfg_meta_description: Take a HireSignal interview yourself. Choose the level, the language and whether to assess your language skills, then get the full report by email.
cfg_lede: Choose how HireSignal should interview you. We email you a link to start, and when you finish, the full report goes to the same inbox.
cfg_s1_why: The level sets the tone and how hard the interview pushes. It always adapts to your answers: a vague one comes back later from another angle, a strong one leads to harder questions.
cfg_l1_more: Warm and conversational, in everyday language. It only gets more direct if answers turn evasive or sound rehearsed.
cfg_l2_more: Warm at first, then more structured and precise as the conversation needs it.
cfg_l3_more: Peer to peer from the first question, and more rigorous as it goes. Expect questions about decisions you made and results you owned.
cfg_s2_why: The interview runs in this language from start to finish, except for the language check below if you turn it on.
cfg_s3_why: Turn it on when a job needs a language. For a few questions the interview switches to each language you pick, and the report gives a level for each one: basic, intermediate, advanced or fluent. When a job requires a language, a basic level shows as a requirement not met, apart from the score.
cfg_s4_why: HireSignal reads the CV before the interview. It uses it to ask about the experience on it and to notice answers that don't match it.
cfg_cv_sample_more: A fictional applicant for the level you picked. Answer as that person. One of the sample CVs hides a trick: see if the report catches it.
cfg_cv_own_more: Answer as yourself. The file is read for this demo and is not kept: only the text goes into the interview.
cfg_s5_why: We send the link to start, and later the report, to this address. Our team sees that you took the demo and may follow up. We don't share your report.
cfg_limits: One try per level for each email. If today's demos are taken, book a time and we'll run one with you.
try_l1_p: Casual tone. Experience, organisation and how you handle a busy day.
try_l2_p: Standard tone. Troubleshooting, and how deep your answers really go.
try_l3_p: Peer tone. Leadership, decisions and results you owned.
try_assess_hint: The interview switches language for a few questions, and the report gives your level in each one.
try_consent: Send me the interview link and my report by email. My answers are used only for this demo.
try_note: About 15 minutes. One try per level.
try_pending: The live demo opens soon. Until then, book a demo and we'll run one with you.
team_title: Built by people who have *done* the hiring.

team_h_bio: 15+ years leading operations and client teams across Latin America and Canada, from frontline agent in Bogotá to senior operations manager in Ontario. He has run teams of 200 and was ranked first worldwide in vendor performance.
team_a_bio: 15+ years in BPO and customer experience operations across Latin America and North America, from frontline agent in Bogotá to regional operations manager, leading teams of 100+ and client portfolios of $50M a year. He built HireSignal.
